---
title: "JSON Resume schema"
description: "The Reactive Resume JSON Schema, published at /schema.json: what it covers, how to validate resume data against it, and how to build on it."
---

## The vision

I want applying for a job to be as simple as sending a JSON file from one service to a job listing portal, without parsing errors, format inconsistencies, or bias from how a resume happens to be laid out.

Reactive Resume aims to be the gold standard in JSON resume schemas: one documented, strictly typed schema that any service can adopt so resumes move between tools without loss.

Imagine:

- Exporting your resume from Reactive Resume as a JSON file
- Uploading it directly to a job portal that instantly understands every field
- No more PDF parsing failures or ATS (Applicant Tracking System) misreads
- Your qualifications evaluated purely on merit, not on formatting quirks

This is the future I'm hoping to build toward.

## The schema endpoint

The Reactive Resume JSON Schema is publicly available at:

<Info>[https://rxresu.me/schema.json](https://rxresu.me/schema.json)</Info>

The endpoint returns a complete JSON Schema in the draft 2020-12 dialect. It describes the structure of a Reactive Resume document and covers:

- **All resume sections**: basics, summary, experience, education, projects, skills, languages, interests, awards, certifications, publications, volunteer work, and references
- **Custom sections**: user-defined sections whose `type` selects one of the documented item shapes
- **Metadata**: template, layout, typography, colors, page settings, and custom CSS
- **Full descriptions**: every field is documented with its purpose and expected format

## Schema dialect and document shape

The schema document declares its JSON Schema dialect in its own `$schema` field:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object"
}
```

Resume documents do not include a top-level `version` property. They also do not include the schema document's
`$schema` field. Validate the exported resume object directly against the canonical schema endpoint.

## Using the schema

### Validating resume data

You can use the schema to validate resume JSON files in any language that supports JSON Schema validation:

```javascript
import Ajv2020 from "ajv/dist/2020.js";

const ajv = new Ajv2020();
const schema = await fetch("https://rxresu.me/schema.json").then((r) => r.json());
const validate = ajv.compile(schema);

const isValid = validate(resumeData);
if (!isValid) {
  console.error(validate.errors);
}
```

### IDE autocompletion

Associate exported resume files with the canonical schema in VS Code's `settings.json`:

```json
{
  "json.schemas": [
    {
      "fileMatch": ["reactive-resume*.json"],
      "url": "https://rxresu.me/schema.json"
    }
  ]
}
```

This keeps editor configuration outside the resume data and avoids adding unsupported top-level properties.

### Building integrations

The schema enables third-party integrations:

- **Job portals** can accept Reactive Resume JSON files directly
- **HR systems** can parse candidate data without lossy PDF conversion
- **Other resume builders** can import/export using a common format
- **AI tools** can understand resume structure for analysis or enhancement

## Schema structure overview

The resume data is organized into these top-level sections:

| Section          | Description                                     |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `picture`        | Profile photo configuration                     |
| `basics`         | Name, headline, contact info, custom fields     |
| `summary`        | Professional summary or bio                     |
| `sections`       | Standard sections (experience, education, etc.) |
| `customSections` | User-defined additional sections                |
| `metadata`       | Template, layout, design, typography settings   |

Each section within `sections` follows a consistent structure:

```json
{
  "title": "Experience",
  "columns": 1,
  "hidden": false,
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "229ad766-cb9a-4f16-aaf0-fdd8394a9b95",
      "hidden": false,
      "company": "Analytical Engines",
      "position": "Engineer",
      "location": "London",
      "period": "1842",
      "website": {
        "url": "",
        "label": "",
        "inlineLink": false
      },
      "description": "<p>Built algorithms.</p>",
      "roles": []
    }
  ]
}
```

## For developers and job portals

If you're building a job portal, HR system, or any other service that handles resumes, I'd encourage you to adopt this schema:

- **Zero parsing errors**: structured data means no OCR or PDF parsing mistakes
- **Complete information**: all resume data is preserved, including links and metadata
- **Easy integration**: JSON is universally supported across all platforms
- **Canonical contract**: one public schema endpoint tracks the current Reactive Resume data model

The schema is open and free to use. Fetch it programmatically, or reference it by URL from your own systems.

## Complete JSON Schema

The full JSON Schema for Reactive Resume follows. You can also fetch the latest version directly from [https://rxresu.me/schema.json](https://rxresu.me/schema.json).

<Tip>Copy the schema from the live endpoint so you always have the latest version.</Tip>
